questions.text:
Consider a 2-way set associative cache with 256 blocks and uses LRU replacement, Initially the cache is empty. Conflict misses are those misses which occur due the contention of multiple blocks for the same cache set. Compulsory misses occur due to first time access to the block. The following sequence of accesses to memory blocks.

(0,128,256,128,0,128,256,128,1,129,257,129,1,129,257,129)

is repeated 10 times. The number of conflict misses experienced by the cache is ___________.
questions.solution:
128 sets (2-way). Blocks 0, 128, 256 map to set 0; 1, 129, 257 map to set 1. Set 0 sees 0, 128, 256, 128, 0, 128, 256, 128 each round:
- Round 1: 0, 128, 256 are compulsory misses; then 0 and 256 miss again (conflict) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 conflict misses.
- Each later round: 0 and 256 keep evicting each other (128 stays) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 conflict misses.

Set 0: 2 + 9 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 38. Set 1 behaves the same: 38. Total = 76

Answer: 76

questions.text:
Consider the expression ( a-1)* (((b + c) / 3) + d)) . Let X be the minimum number of
registers required by an optimal code generation (without any register spill) algorithm for a
load/store architecture in which (i) only loads and store instructions can have memory
operands and (ii) arithmetic instructions can have only register or immediate operands. The
value of X is _________.
questions.solution:
Evaluate the bigger subtree first:
- R1 = b, R2 = c, R1 = R1 + R2, R1 = R1 / 3, R2 = d, R1 = R1 + R2
- R2 = a, R2 = R2 [latex]-[/latex] 1, R1 = R2 * R1

Only 2 registers are ever needed.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
A cache memory unit with capacity of N words and block size of B words is to be designed.
If it is designed as a direct mapped cache, the length of the TAG field is 10 bits. If the cache
unit is now designed as a 16-way set-associative cache, the length of the TAG field is
______bits.
questions.solution:
Direct mapped: N/B lines. 16-way: (N/B)/16 sets, i.e. 16 = [latex]2^4[/latex] times fewer sets [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the index loses 4 bits, which go to the tag.

Tag = 10 + 4 = 14 bits

Answer: 14

total(v) adds the number of 1-bits of v to a static count that is never reset, and returns it.
- i = 5 (101): count = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 2
- i = 4 (100): count = 3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 5
- i = 3 (11): count = 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 10
- i = 2 (10): count = 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 16
- i = 1 (1): count = 7 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = 23

Answer: 23
